title: County of Tripoli
capsule: The County of Tripoli was a Crusader state on the Levantine coast, founded in 1102 when Bertrand of Toulouse captured the city of Tripoli after a prolonged siege supported by a Genoese fleet — the Genoese received roughly a quarter of the city and surrounding land as payment. The county functioned as a feudal vassal of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, stretching at its height from Maraclea in the north to near Beirut in the south; in 1144 Count Raymond II granted the Knights Hospitaller the frontier fortress of Krak des Chevaliers and adjacent lands to defend against Muslim pressure. The county's strategic miscalculation of allying with the Mongols against Mamluk Egypt led the Mamluk sultan Qalawun to conquer Tripoli on 27 April 1289, with the last count Lucia unable to mount effective resistance; the city was razed and its population enslaved.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's coastal extent is moderately well attested through Crusader chronicles and Genoese commercial records, but its inland limits against Muslim principalities fluctuated and are not precisely documented.
